title: Distinct-event counts retained a grid-sensitive deep-earthquake excess in monthly ComCat tests for 2000-2025
abstract: We tested whether a published deep-earthquake pair excess also occurs in the number of distinct events in close pairs. We used 785 ComCat events with preferred magnitude at least 5.5 and depth greater than 300 km in 2000-2025. A pair must be within 200 km chord distance and seven days in the same year. There were 175 pairs with 170 distinct events. Monthly time shuffles within twenty-degree cells gave a mean of 160.91 distinct events and an upper-tail p value of 0.0154 in 9,999 draws. Ten-degree controls gave 165.88 and p = 0.0678. Thus counting each event once did not remove the primary residual, but geographic control still changed the test result. The largest component had ten events and was ten in every primary draw. This is a graph-based check on reused records, not independent evidence for triggering. Sparse monthly groups, exchangeability, catalog error and grid choice limit the result. Code, aggregate draws, source hashes, a figure and a separate numerical audit are included. External event records are excluded.

display.caption: Observed pair and distinct-event counts against conditional shuffle means and central 95% null ranges. These ranges are not effect confidence intervals.

citations.reason: Published monthly pair result set the new distinct-event question. The source records overlap; this is not independent confirmation.
